summary.text: 爸 means “father” or “papa.” It is analyzed as a compound: 父 contributes the father meaning, and 巴 is proposed as a sound component.

formation.text: Phonosemantic: 父 contributes meaning and 巴 is proposed as a sound cue. In Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese reconstruction, 巴 is *praː and 爸 is *praːs, a comparison supporting the proposed sound role. 巴’s original referent and name remain disputed, so they cannot independently confirm this analysis.

components.text: 父 contributes the meaning “father.” A transmitted Shuowen account describes 父 as a family head holding a staff, but this account does not establish 父’s original pictorial meaning within 爸. The selected oracle-style image is a modern redraw of 父 alone, not an early form of 爸.

巴 is proposed as the sound component. The Shuowen tradition links 巴 to a giant snake; another proposal reads early forms identified as 巴 as a kneeling person. Neither referent or name is established. The selected oracle-style image is a modern redraw of 巴 alone, not an attestation of 爸.

sound.text: In Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese reconstruction, 巴 *praː is compared with 爸 *praːs. This supports the proposed sound role; the disputed identity and original referent of early 巴 do not independently confirm the comparison.

history.text: 爸 is absent from Shuowen. Guangya groups 爸 with 爹 and 㸙 under the gloss “father”; this records use of the word, not when the graph was formed. The selected oracle-style images show 父 and 巴 separately and do not establish an earlier form or graphic sequence for 爸.

A historical dictionary preserves an account in which 父 was added to a father word written 八八 or 巴巴. A later study instead argues that the father word is phonologically from 父. These competing explanations do not establish how or when the graph was formed.

uncertainties.text: The phonosemantic analysis is reported, but no early inscription or dated sequence of the complete graph shows when 父 and 巴 were combined.

巴’s early form and referent are disputed: the Shuowen tradition associates it with a giant snake, while another proposal interprets forms identified as 巴 as a kneeling person. This leaves its original name unsettled and prevents independent confirmation of the proposed sound comparison in 爸.

The proposed Proto-Sino-Tibetan source for the father word and the claim that 爸 preserves an older pronunciation of 父 are not independently substantiated here. These lexical claims are separate from the proposed 巴 sound component.

senses.period: Three Kingdoms era (reported dating of the Guangya record)
senses.text: A Guangya entry is reported to gloss 爸 as “father.” This records use of the word, though it does not provide a dated physical witness for the graph.
Modern references gloss 爸 as “father” and “papa”; no separate historical stage for “papa” is established.

limitations.text: The recorded “father” gloss does not date the graph’s formation, and no chronological development from “father” to “papa” is established.

overview.text: 爸 means “father” or “papa.” In the proposed sound analysis, 父 contributes the meaning and 巴 supplies a sound cue; the comparison is supported by a Zhengzhang Old Chinese reconstruction, while 巴’s original referent remains disputed.

components.text: 父 contributes the father meaning. Its selected oracle-style image is a modern redraw of 父 alone, not an early 爸.
巴 is proposed as the sound component. Its original referent is disputed, but the proposed sound comparison has reconstructed support.

relationships.text: 父 contributes the father meaning in the reported phonosemantic analysis of 爸.
巴 is proposed as a sound component, compared with 爸 as *praː and *praːs respectively in Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese system. The identity and original referent of early 巴 remain unsettled.
